prompt: Put Google Play's tracks in order, from the smallest audience to the largest.
Why does the ladder of tracks exist, in the lesson's words?

choices.text: To satisfy Google's review
choices.why: Most tracks are reviewed anyway; that is not the purpose.

choices.text: To keep competitors from seeing new features
choices.why: Open testing is visible to anybody.

choices.text: So the first person to meet a crash is the cheapest one
choices.why: Right. Each rung widens the audience and the cost of a bug.

choices.text: Because production allows one release a month
choices.why: No such limit exists.

prompt: Ana is a tester on the internal and the closed tracks. Internal holds version code 50; closed holds 52. Which does she get?

choices.why: Right. The highest code among the tracks she can see.

choices.text: Both, as two apps
choices.why: Same package, one install.

choices.text: 50, because internal is her team's track
choices.why: Tracks have no priority; the code decides.

choices.text: Whichever she opted into last
choices.why: Order of joining does not matter.

prompt: How many testers can Google Play's internal track hold?
A tester returns from four months away and the planner's TestFlight build will not open. What happened?

choices.text: App Review withdrew it
choices.why: Nothing suggests a withdrawal; the calendar explains it.

choices.text: The tester's phone lost its registration
choices.why: TestFlight needs no device registration.

choices.text: The distribution certificate was renewed
choices.why: Renewing does not stop a build that Apple re-signed.

choices.text: The build passed its 90 days and expired
choices.why: Right. Testing builds open for 90 days.

prompt: Match each fact to the kind of TestFlight tester.

pairs.left: needs a role in App Store Connect
the first build sent to their group is reviewed

prompt: Why does a public TestFlight link have a limit on how many people it admits?

choices.text: Apple charges per tester
choices.why: Testers are free.

choices.text: So a link shared on a forum does not take every place
choices.why: Right. The external limit is ten thousand in all.

choices.text: The link expires after the limit
choices.why: It stops admitting, which is the point.

choices.text: Internal testers need the remaining places
choices.why: Internal testers have their own hundred.

prompt: In `tracks.ts`, why was the second upload of code 42 refused?

choices.text: Production accepts only promoted builds
choices.why: Production accepts uploads; the code was the problem.

choices.text: Code 42 had been uploaded before
choices.why: Right. A version code is used once, on any track.

choices.text: Carla was not a tester
choices.why: People have nothing to do with uploads.

choices.text: 43 was higher
choices.why: A lower code is refused only on a track already holding a higher one; here the code was reused.

prompt: A release manager wants to rebuild the beta's commit with a fresh version code and send that to production, "to be clean". What is the objection?

choices.text: Google refuses rebuilt commits
choices.why: Google cannot tell; a new code would be accepted.

choices.text: The new build would be signed with another key
choices.why: The same upload key would sign it.

choices.text: None; a rebuild of the same commit is the same build
choices.why: Toolchains and dependencies drift; it is a binary nobody tested.

choices.text: Production then gets a binary the testers never ran
choices.why: Right. Promote the build that was tested.

prompt: In Fastlane, `upload_to_play_store` with `___` moves a release to another track without uploading anything.
Which closed-beta tester will find the most for the planner?

choices.text: A student using it for their real term
choices.why: Right. Real use finds what nobody planned.

choices.text: A colleague with a test account named Course 1
choices.why: Test data finds what the team already knew.

choices.text: A stranger who installs and uninstalls the same day
choices.why: Too little use to find much.

choices.text: The developer who wrote the feature
choices.why: They test what they meant, not what others do.

prompt: What does the lesson say should go out with each beta build?

choices.text: A survey of twenty questions
choices.why: Long surveys go unanswered.

choices.text: Nothing, so testers are not biased
choices.why: Then testers do not know what to look at.

choices.text: A sentence saying what changed and what to try
choices.why: Right. What to Test and the track's release notes are for it.

choices.text: The full changelog of every commit
choices.why: Testers need one question, not a log.

prompt: A beta ran for three weeks with no reported problems, and the release crashes on one phone model in production. What does that show?

choices.text: A beta finds what its people notice on their phones, and no more
choices.why: Right. That is why production is released in stages.

choices.text: The testers were careless
choices.why: They could only find what their phones showed.

choices.text: Betas are useless
choices.why: They found what they could; they cannot find everything.

choices.text: The build was rebuilt before production
choices.why: Nothing says so; the model was simply not in the beta.

prompt: The planner's Android team uploads every build straight to production. Which rung of the ladder would have saved them most?

choices.text: A second production account
choices.why: That is not a rung, and it splits the app.

choices.text: Open testing, used once a year
choices.why: Once a year misses almost every build.

choices.text: Internal testing, used on every build
choices.why: Right. The cheapest person meets the crash first.

choices.text: None; production is tested by its users
choices.why: That is the expensive way to find out.

prompt: Which of these does a React Native team run when it tests both platforms? Choose every one.

choices.text: TestFlight for the iOS build
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Play's testing tracks for the Android build
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A shared beta service run by the stores for both
choices.why: There is none; two ladders side by side.

choices.text: Ad hoc builds for every Android tester
choices.why: Ad hoc is an iOS idea.
